before.exam_tip_html: When describing rock music in a listening question, avoid vague words like “loud” or “heavy.” Instead, use precise musical vocabulary: say the guitar uses distortion, the chords are power chords (root and 5th only, neither major nor minor), or the opening is based on a riff. If you can hear a sound more in one ear, describe it as panned to the left or right. Examiners reward correct terminology — the more specific you are, the more marks you earn.

In listening questions on musical theatre, the examiner wants you to explain how the music creates a specific effect — not just what happens. Always use this formula: identify the musical feature (e.g. “a crescendo in the strings”), then explain its effect (e.g. “which builds tension as the character reaches her decision”). Use correct musical vocabulary such as texture, dynamics, articulation, and structure. When describing how parts interact, mention specific instruments or voices and explain whether they are playing in unison, harmony, imitation, or call and response. This is what separates good answers from great ones in AoS2.
